messages:
zoe: Heads-up: POC customer (NimbusEdge) rotated keys and now getting 401/403 intermittently. Started at ~11:02 UTC. Can we swarm?

alex: pinging infra for request ids. Are they hitting streaming endpoints or embeddings?

zoe: embeddings + responses. They said it worked in dev but failing in staging. They pasted this curl: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_poc_NEW\" -d '{\"input\":\"hey\"}'` -> `{\"error\":\"unauthorized\",\"message\":\"invalid credentials\"}`

carter: found request_id=aa12c3 in auth logs. entry: `warn auth: bind_failed token=sk_poc_NEW err=header_missing x-rw-org`. Looks like headers stripped by their proxy.

ivy: they mentioned using a short-lived corporate proxy (env: PROXY_URL) that rewrites auth headers for logging. if the proxy drops `x-rw-org` we will fallback to token binding which might differ.

alex: easiest repro: ask them to curl the api directly bypassing proxy or to explicitly include `x-rw-org` and `x-rw-project`. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_poc_NEW" \
  -H "x-rw-org: nimbus-edge" \
  -H "x-rw-project: nimbus-stg" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"probe"}'
```

sec-bot: automated: token-rotation logged key_id=sk_poc_NEW user=zoe@redwood at 2026-03-21T11:00:12Z.

zoe: customer tried adding headers but still saw failures from some clients behind proxy. they confirmed some mobile clients can't set custom headers.

carter: two options: 1) create a token bound to the canonical org alias that matches the proxy default (so header not required), or 2) instruct proxy to forward headers or use project-id binding via query param/internal mapping. binding by project id avoids human-readable slug issues.

ivy: security note: for option 1 we can create a service key `allowed_orgs: [\"nimbus-edge\", \"nimbus-edge-staging\"]` with a 48h TTL for POC. prefer issuing a new service key vs broadening an existing prod key.

alex: also verify scopes: logs show token_scopes=[embed:read-lite] and endpoint requires embed:read. that would cause 403 with `insufficient_scope`. but current logs show header_missing first. multi-cause.

zoe: asked customer to run a direct curl from a laptop (bypass proxy) and they got 200 with request_id=aa12d0. confirmed proxy is the culprit.

carter: created new service key `sk_poc_proxy_1` with scopes=[embed:read, generate:basic] allowed_orgs=[\"nimbus-edge\"] TTL=72h. posted via secure channel per sec guidance.

sec-bot: automated: service-key-created id=sk_poc_proxy_1 created_by=ivy@redwood note=\"poc temporary key\" ttl=72h.

ivy: approved. audit entry added. Also recommended they rotate keys post-POC and avoid embedding PII in requests while proxy logs are enabled.

alex: customer also asked about Dedicated pricing if they want to drive consistent embed throughput. AE to follow up on quote. For presales notes: dedicated starts at $Yk/month, adds reserved GPU pool + SLA, discuss burst pricing.

zoe: customer accepted temporary key and validated across clients. they will disable header rewriting on the proxy for staging. they also asked how we recommend storing keys client-side for mobile.

carter: advise: never embed prod keys in mobile apps; use short-lived service tokens issued by a backend auth service + rotation. add this to SQA.

zoe: wrapping up: auth fixed by issuing scoped service key and proxy change. AE (@ivy) to confirm quote. i'll follow up with rotation/revoke steps once POC ends. :thumbsup:

auth-bot: automated: request_id=aa12d0 validated for token=sk_poc_proxy_1 status=accepted

sec-bot: automated: revocation-plan scheduled reminder in 7 days for key=sk_poc_proxy_1
